facts.fact: A brown, quick river runs below the lower narrows past a shingle bank where the cut meets the cart road; the near (Varanad) bank has thorn below the shelf.
facts.why: needed because the beat has a creature swim the river and climb out below the narrows.

facts.fact: Muthu brought eleven sheaves of arrows (forty to a sheaf) down the cut by handcart at midmorning.
facts.why: gives Devan a reason to be counting arrows on the shelf and Muthu a reason to be present as witness.

facts.fact: The queen's letter to Devan is in a clerk's round hand with a few closing lines in her own slanting hand ('You will think it a lever. It is.'); it states that the same offer is put to Neela in Kodiyur.
facts.why: carries the offer in the beat; the round hand echoes the clerk's hand of F504/F808 (clue).

facts.fact: Devan seals his reply with a bead of plain black wax and the print of his left thumb, because Muthu holds the iron disc; Muthu signs as witness.
facts.why: he has no seal after giving up the office.

facts.fact: A flat Thurai supply cart behind the siege tower carries a small, fresh yellow bird painted on its tailboard (echo of F791).
facts.why: clue plant for the reinterpretation of the yellow bird/sunbird.

facts.fact: Koman reads scent and says the creature that swam the river is not any shape the Resin House ever made; he calls Devan 'warden' and Devan lets him.
facts.why: the watcher in the beat has no scent he can name for the animal.

facts.fact: Members of the Company have begun asking each other whom they would self-name to; Kuttu asked Vellan, who refused.
facts.why: context for Vellan's line about not binding to anyone.
